assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties and stabilities far beyond the microwave definition of the second, using the magic-wavelength idea to cancel lattice light shifts while many atoms are interrogated in parallel. The discovery is a clear, concrete advance in what can be measured and how accurately, and it opens relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and searches for dark matter and varying constants. From an atomic-physics and laser-spectroscopy viewpoint this is a very strong, clean example of an invention with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock. Ye's group drove it to the highest accuracy and stability, and to the many-body regime, and the two are the natural pair. Others (for example Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, Derevianko and the broader lattice-clock community) contributed, but the supplied credit supports a two-person prize, and the Hall and Hänsch comb prize partly overlaps the Ye lineage.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Several independent groups (Japan, the US, Europe, China) operate lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level, with international comparisons and a roadmap towards a redefinition of the second. Timely, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2005 frequency-comb recognition, in which Ye's mentor John Hall shared; a committee might see this as a continuation.
Ion-clock work (Wineland's 2012 recognition) and the single-ion optical clock priority are adjacent, and I rely on memory for the detailed priority history.
A formal redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, and the weight of the application impact is still partly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brings strong coupling between a single photon in a resonator and a controllable artificial atom onto a chip, with dispersive readout and the transmon forming the basis of the leading superconducting quantum-processor platform. The concept transfers cavity QED, which I know well, to a solid-state setting, and the experimental clarity and engineering consequence are outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal and the 2004 strong-coupling demonstration. Of the supplied names, Schoelkopf and Wallraff led the experiments and Blais the key theory. A fair three-person configuration exists, though Girvin, Devoret and Koch (transmon) are not in the credited list and the allocation relative to the 2025 recognition of superconducting-circuit quantum behaviour is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent confirmation by many groups and extension to commercial devices. Recognition is timely, but the prize adjacent to this field may reduce the chance of a close repeat.
uncertainties: Proximity to prior circuit-quantum-mechanics recognition (I am uncertain exactly how the committee framed that earlier prize).
Credit overlap with the transmon inventors and with Devoret and Girvin, who are not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single colour-centre spins, above all the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, combine optical initialisation and readout with long coherence at room temperature. They give a new class of quantum sensor for magnetic fields, temperature and strain at nanometre scale, plus spin-photon interfaces. This sits close to my own interests in optical addressing of solid-state spins and in measurement limits, and the sensing impact is real.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first detected and manipulated single NV centres optically (1997 onwards) and later demonstrated coherent control and nuclear-spin registers. Awschalom extended this to the wider colour-centre family (SiC, divacancies) and to coherent control at high speed. Lukin is also credited but would take a fourth place; the three-person choice is defensible, with Lukin's sensing and register work a genuine competing claim.
assessment.maturity: Largely mature in the NV case, with extensive replication and early commercial sensors. The SiC and other colour-centre extensions are younger and less settled.
uncertainties: Which parts of the compound topic (single-spin detection, sensing, quantum registers, other defects) the prize should cover.
Choice among four credited names, with Lukin excluded by the three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable Hubbard-type models. The superfluid-to-Mott transition, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes and quantum simulation of many-body dynamics have created a new experimental way to study strongly correlated quantum matter. Importance and originality are high, and this is atomic physics at its best.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch and Zoller proposal motivated the optical-lattice Hubbard simulator, Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition, and Bloch and Greiner developed the quantum gas microscope. Cirac and Zoller are also credited, and Zoller's inclusion rewards the theory. Jaksch is not on the list and the picture is complex because Cirac and Zoller overlap with other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the observation of the Mott insulator and microscopy. Quantum-simulation claims of exceeding classical methods are still developing, so the strongest recognition is for the experimental platform rather than for a final scientific payoff.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 and 1997 recognitions of Bose-Einstein condensation and laser cooling, which may make a committee cautious.
Whether the prize is for the platform, the Mott demonstration or quantum simulation, and who among Bloch, Greiner, Cirac and Zoller is core.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution, from BB84 to Ekert's entanglement-based protocol, turned quantum measurement and no-cloning into a cryptographic principle. It is conceptually original, linked to Bell tests and to the information view of quantum mechanics, and has a large experimental and technological footprint with fibre and satellite links.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the BB84 originators and Ekert independently introduced the E91 entanglement-based scheme, so the supplied three names form a coherent trio. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known precursor and he is not credited here, and experimental builders such as Gisin and Pan are separate candidates.
assessment.maturity: The theory is decades old and well accepted. Experimental demonstrations are extensive, though practical security (device imperfections, side channels) remains an active qualification, and the physics versus information-science character is a question for the committee.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel physics criteria are met by protocols whose main impact is cryptographic.
Overlap with the 2022 recognition of entanglement and Bell tests, and with long-distance communication experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the experiments by Blatt and others showed how laser-controlled ions can implement universal quantum logic with high fidelity. It is a founding pillar of experimental quantum information in atomic physics, and a very concrete route to large-scale operation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 theoretical proposal, and Blatt's group demonstrated key gates, entanglement and algorithms. Wineland's group did important early gate and entanglement work, and Wineland was recognised in 2012 for ion control, so the experimental credit is spread across several groups that are not all in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent verification in multiple laboratories and commercial processors. Timing is reasonable, but the earlier ion-trap recognition reduces room for a further prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for single-quantum-system control, and the credit position of Wineland, Monroe and others.
Cirac and Zoller also appear under two other candidates, so a prize configuration across those entries could be inconsistent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a large new field with tunable strongly correlated physics. The idea is original and the impact is broad, though it is outside my own specialty and I weigh it with some humility.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experiments. The pairing of prediction and discovery is clean, though the supplied names omit other contributors such as Cao, Fatemi, and Dean and colleagues on related moire work, and others in the field might claim parts of the credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably confirmed by many independent groups, yet the field is young, the interpretation of superconductivity is not settled and the long-term lasting stability is not yet clear.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity and some correlated phases remains debated.
Whether the field is mature enough, and whether the credit should include experimental co-authors not on the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms interacting through Rydberg states, built from optical tweezers, provide a flexible platform for quantum simulation and quantum computation, with entangling gates and observation of new quantum phases. It is an elegant application of laser cooling, tweezers and Rydberg blockade, with strong experimental originality.
assessment.attribution: Browaeys's and Lukin's groups made leading demonstrations of tweezer arrays and many-body Rydberg physics, and Saffman contributed key proposals and gate demonstrations. Credit is spread across a number of groups, including Bloch, Greiner, Endres, Lahaye and others, and it is a compound development with rapid current progress. A two-name proposal is a weak fit for the breadth of contributors.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young, though quickly confirmed by multiple groups. The long-term significance and which results will prove the decisive ones are not yet clear, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Premature compared with more settled atomic-physics topics, and the decisive contributions are not yet crystallised.
Overlap in credit among optical tweezer, Rydberg-blockade and quantum-simulation lines of work.
